subject: Internal hostnames & certificate flow for split-horizon private endpoints
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-healthcare.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on TLS termination & internal hostnames for private endpoints

Hi Tessa / Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Security team had a few follow-ups specific to our private deployment:

- Where does TLS terminate in each supported deployment mode (VPC peering, customer edge proxy, or Redwood ingress)?
- If TLS terminates inside customer network, how do we handle SANs for internal hostnames (e.g. api.internal.acme)? Can Redwood accept certs that include RFC1918 IPs or internal DNS names?
- Do you support mutual TLS for service-to-service calls into the on-prem runtime?
- Rotation: what is the recommended process for cert rotation and can we push certs to Redwood via an API / SFTP / onboarding bundle?

I've attached a short list of our policy requirements (acme_tls_questions.docx). Can we get a compact recommendation matrix and a short diagram showing the handshake flow for the recommended approach?

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Security Architect
Acme Healthcare

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-healthcare.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on TLS termination & internal hostnames for private endpoints

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary + three viable patterns and a recommended default. Attaching a sketch (tls_flow_sketch.png).

1) Customer-edge termination (recommended for highest isolation)
   - TLS terminates at the customer's perimeter/load‑balancer.
   - Redwood receives plaintext over private peering or a mutually authenticated tunnel (mTLS).
   - Pros: customer retains private keys; easiest to meet strict compliance.
   - Cons: requires customer-side routing and potentially NAT/port mapping; Redwood SDKs need mTLS support on enterprise plan.

2) Split-horizon DNS + Redwood ingress termination (recommended default for most customers)
   - DNS inside customer VPC resolves private hostnames to internal IPs (split-horizon). Public DNS points to Redwood-hosted endpoints.
   - Customer uploads/manages certs (SNI) to Redwood Private or uses ACME with DNS challenge via delegated zone.
   - Pros: simpler for app teams, allows Redwood-managed rotation if customer opts in.
   - Cons: customer must allow near-real-time rotation paths and provide delegated DNS or upload tooling.

3) End-to-end mTLS passthrough (for service-to-service auth)
   - TLS passthrough to service sidecars; mTLS handled between client and service.
   - Pros: full E2E integrity.
   - Cons: operational complexity and limited observability for some Redwood features (e.g., request-level tracing).

Notes on SANs / internal names:
- We do not sign certs that include RFC1918 addresses on hosted public CA certs. For internal hostnames you have two options: (a) use customer-managed certs including those internal SANs and upload them to the Private control plane, or (b) run an internal CA and configure Redwood Private to trust that CA (via supplied root certificate).

Rotation options:
- Customer push: upload via our Private API or SFTP (we support both).
- ACME: Redwood can use DNS-01 if you delegate a subzone.
- Manual: upload in Console / DocuSign contract (short-term).

I'll loop in Hiro to confirm the technical constraints and Karthik for DNS guidance. Can we set up a 30-min review Wednesday?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-healthcare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on TLS termination & internal hostnames for private endpoints

On Mon, Aug 2, 2026 at 12:30 PM Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll loop in Hiro to confirm the technical constraints and Karthik for DNS guidance.

Quick technical notes from infra:

- Mutual TLS:
  * We support client cert validation at the ingress layer for Redwood Private (Envoy). We can require client certs for specific routes and validate against a CA bundle you provide.
  * For VPC peering / private-link style connections, we recommend mTLS terminated at the customer edge when you need full key ownership.

- Certificate storage & rotation:
  * Customer-managed certs are stored encrypted in customer-specific key stores (KMS-backed). Private operators can install HSM-backed keys for rotation.
  * Rotation modes: API-driven (recommended), scheduled auto-rotate (via ACME + DNS), and manual.

- SANs and internal names:
  * Redwood will accept certs that include internal DNS names if you upload them or provide a signing CA we trust. We do not offer public CA issuance for RFC1918 names.
  * If you need wildcard coverage for *.internal.acme, upload a wildcard cert and enable internal DNS split-horizon. Beware wildcard certs and coverage of sub-subdomains.

- TLS termination implications for observability/traceability:
  * Termination at Redwood ingress gives us request-level tracing, per-token cost and latency visibility, and easier rollout control.
  * Termination at customer edge preserves keys but reduces our ability to provide fine-grained observability; we provide hooks for logging plaintext metadata over the private channel if that helps compliance.

Action items for the call:
- Confirm whether Acme wants Redwood to manage rotation or prefer customer push.
- Decide on split-horizon DNS approach and whether you can delegate a subzone for ACME DNS-01.
- Confirm whether you need mTLS for all upstream calls or just for control plane.

-Hiro
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-healthcare.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on TLS termination & internal hostnames for private endpoints

Hi Alice — adding a couple procurement/ops points from our side:

- Responsibility matrix: we should include a clear SOW line for cert rotation (if Redwood manages rotation, include hours & runbook + emergency rotation SLA).
- Escrow/backup: some healthcare customers ask Redwood to escrow certs in a sealed KMS; that's possible under enterprise terms (we'll need legal sign-off).
- Audits: we can provide rotation logs and KMS audit trails as part of a SOC2 evidence bundle.

I'll open a Jira (INFRA-4217) to track the implementation steps and a short playbook we can share. Also looping procurement@acme-healthcare.com for billing implications if you opt into Managed Rotation.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-healthcare.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T09:00:00Z
Subject: Plan: Redwood ingress with customer-managed certs + optional mTLS (proposed)

Alice — thanks everyone for quick inputs. Proposed approach for our review call:

- Default proposal (Option B): Redwood ingress termination with customer-supplied certs.
  * Customer uploads certs (PEM) via Private API or delegates a subzone for ACME DNS-01.
  * Redwood stores certs in KMS; rotation can be managed by customer push or Redwood-managed ACME if delegated.
  * Optional mTLS: require client certs per-route; we validate against customer-provided CA bundle.

- Fallback: Customer-edge termination for workloads requiring absolute key custody.

Deliverables for Wednesday call:
- Short diagram (attached previously) showing DNS split-horizon and handshake flow.
- Cert responsibility matrix (I'll attach redwood_private_cert_matrix.xlsx).
- Proposed SOW language for Managed Rotation (Monica to draft).

Please confirm if Wednesday 2026-08-04 16:00 UTC works for you. If approved, we'll produce the 1-page runbook + Jira tasks.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
